choices.title: 3
choices.correct_explanation:
• Muscle strength is assessed using the Medical Research Council (MRC) scale, a universally accepted 0–5 point scale.
  • A score of 3 means the patient is able to:
    • Move the limb against gravity, but
    • Not able to move it against any resistance applied by the examiner.
  • In this case, since the patient can move the limb normally (against gravity) but cannot resist external force, it fits exactly into Grade 3 on the MRC scale.

MRC Muscle Strength Grading Scale Recap:

Grade

Description

0

No visible or palpable muscle contraction

1

Muscle flicker or trace contraction, but no movement

2

Active movement only with gravity eliminated (e.g., side-lying)

3

Active movement against gravity but not against resistance

4

Active movement against some resistance

5

Normal strength – active movement against full resistance

Explanation of Distractors:

a) Grade 1 –

  • Only trace muscle contraction, but no visible limb movement.
  • This patient is clearly able to move the limb, so this is too low.

b) Grade 2 –

  • Movement is possible only when gravity is eliminated, i.e., horizontal plane movement.
  • Since the patient can move limbs in normal vertical directions (against gravity), this grade is not appropriate.

d) Grade 4 –

  • Movement is possible against some resistance applied by the examiner.
  • But this patient fails to move against any resistance, so Grade 4 is too high.

Clinical Tip:

  • Always test muscle strength symmetrically and compare bilaterally.
  • Muscle strength evaluation helps localize neurological lesions, identify motor neuron diseases, or monitor recovery post-stroke or injury.

• A swelling in the midline of the neck that moves on deglutition (swallowing) is a characteristic sign of structures physically attached to the larynx or the thyroid gland. 
    Thyroglossal Cysts and Thyroid Nodules (especially those in the isthmus) are classically known to move with deglutition because they are either part of the thyroid gland or connected to the hyoid bone/larynx via embryonic remnants.
  • Subhyoid bursitis involves the bursa between the hyoid bone and the thyroid cartilage; because of this close anatomical proximity and attachment to the laryngeal framework, it can also move during swallowing.

choices.title: In neurogenic shock, the skin is warm and dry
choices.correct_explanation:
• To differentiate Neurogenic shock from Hypovolemic shock, focus on skin temperature and heart rate:

Neurogenic Shock:

  • Cause: Loss of sympathetic tone (e.g., spinal cord injury)
  • Skin: Warm, dry (due to vasodilation)
  • Heart rate: Bradycardia (unique feature)
  • Blood vessels: Dilated → pooling of blood
  • Because sympathetic control is lost, vessels dilate and skin feels warm, unlike other shocks.

Hypovolemic Shock:

  • Cause: Blood/fluid loss
  • Skin: Cold, clammy
  • Heart rate: Tachycardia (body compensates)
  • Capillary refill: Delayed (>2 sec)
  • Body tries to maintain circulation → vasoconstriction → cold skin
  • B: Hypovolemic shock has tachycardia, not bradycardia
  • C: Capillary refill is delayed, not <2 sec
  • D: Neurogenic shock usually has normal or rapid refill due to vasodilation

In hypovolemic shock, capillary refill is less than 2 seconds
In neurogenic shock, there is delayed capillary refill

The patient is a farmer who developed symptoms while fumigating crops, indicating exposure to pesticides. He presents with a cluster of cholinergic symptoms such as excessive salivation, vomiting, diarrhea, involuntary defecation, bradycardia (pulse 46/min), hypotension, and constricted pupils (miosis). These features are characteristic of organophosphate toxicity, which occurs due to inhibition of acetylcholinesterase, leading to accumulation of acetylcholine and overstimulation of the parasympathetic nervous system.

Answering a Question

  1. Each question will have four options, out of which only one must be selected.
  2. You will receive 1 mark for every correct answer, and 0.33 mark (1/3rd) will be deducted for each incorrect answer.
  3. Click the option you want to mark, in case you want to another question simply select another option the first selection will be automatically omitted.
  4. To attempt the next question click on next to attempt the previous Question click on previous
  5. You can bookmark the Question or also report a question
